contentText: North Korea has modified its national flag as part of a constitutional amendment. The text also enshrined the country's status as a nuclear power and removed any reference to the "peaceful reunification" pursued by Kim Jong Un's predecessors. Meanwhile, the reclusive leader has been keen to demonstrate his desire to expand diplomatic ties with friendly nations. Yuka Royer speaks with Edward Howell of Oxford University to put these recent developments into context.
